supersedes.reason: The first 2.34.5 run was recorded with a process observer that counted an execve-window read as a thread-restriction violation, which set ffmpegThreadRestrictionProven to false. Issue #58 fixed the observer and this record replaces that run in place, as the same anchor. The superseded run measured ffmpegProcessPeak 1 with ffmpegWithoutThreadRestrictionObserved false; that FFmpeg observation is not reproduced here and is not claimed by this record.

alertThresholds.scope: this exact disposable topology and package chain

processObserver.method: docker top every 100 ms. A packaged yt-dlp or FFmpeg process whose argv the kernel has not published yet is reported as an unwritten-argv read and excluded from the restriction counts in both directions; every process with a written argv is checked on the sample that saw it.
processObserver.invariantUnchanged: The kernel publishes the argument vector in one step, so a sampled row is either the bracketed comm or a complete command line and never half of one, and a real invocation of either program always carries a full argument vector. The node builds --postprocessor-args ffmpeg:-threads 1 into its only yt-dlp spawn unconditionally, so a genuinely unrestricted process is measurable the first time it is sampled and still fails the lane however briefly it runs. Only a process the observer cannot measure at all is excluded, and an unmeasured process is not evidence of a violation.
processObserver.unwrittenArgvReadsAreNotPasses: Unwritten-argv reads are reported as ytDlpArgvUnwrittenTotal and ffmpegArgvUnwrittenTotal and are never folded into ytDlpWithoutFfmpegThreadRestrictionObserved, ffmpegWithoutThreadRestrictionObserved, or ffmpegThreadRestrictionProven.
processObserver.ffmpegEvidenceLimit: This run sampled no packaged FFmpeg process at all (ffmpegProcessPeak 0), so ffmpegThreadRestrictionProven rests on the yt-dlp command lines, which carry the restriction the node passes to FFmpeg, and not on a directly sampled FFmpeg process. The lane's acceptance flag did not require an FFmpeg process to be sampled when this run was recorded; since issue #68 it does, and this run would not earn the boolean under the current lane. What is still indirect here is the FFmpeg claim itself: only the argv the node passes to yt-dlp was observed, never FFmpeg honouring it.

decision.supportedScope: worker concurrency 1 until a lower-concurrency disposable load lane passes
